protocol.instrument_name: Enhanced Access Community Pharmacy Pilot - Gastro-oesophageal reflux and gastro-oesophageal reflux disease - Clinical practice guideline
protocol.instrument_version: No version number or date printed (page 9 footer codes read "62'GUA" and "180510-DEC"); © Department of Health 2026
protocol.effective_date: Not printed (© Department of Health 2026; Produced by Clinical Excellence Division)
protocol.legal_basis: Medicines and Poisons Regulations 2016 (WA): 'This clinical practice guideline may only be used by pharmacists who have been approved by the Department of Health to participate in the Enhanced Access Community Pharmacy Pilot (EACPP) and are authorised to prescribe under the Medicines and Poisons Regulations 2016 (WA). This document alone does not provide an authorisation for a pharmacist to prescribe.' (p.1)
protocol.supervision_model: Approved/authorised pharmacist prescribing under the EACPP (document's own terminology) with professional-judgement oversight: 'Pharmacists must exercise professional discretion and judgement consistent with their qualifications and legislative authority. This guideline does not override the responsibility of the pharmacist to undertake clinical assessments and to make decisions appropriate to the circumstances of the individual and the relevant standards of care, in consultation with the patient and/or their parent/caregiver.' (p.1). 'Pharmacists must ensure that they are prescribing medicines according to the specified sections of the current online version of the Therapeutic Guidelines.' (p.6)
protocol.scope_summary: EACPP clinical practice guideline for gastro-oesophageal reflux and gastro-oesophageal reflux disease (GORD), service restricted to patients aged 18 to 55 years (p.1). Guideline overview flow (p.2): meet service and professional obligations (eligibility, consent) -> patient history and assessment (history plus examination of vital signs where appropriate) -> develop management plan (non-pharmacological dietary/lifestyle measures plus pharmacotherapy as per Therapeutic Guidelines: Gastrointestinal) -> confirm management is appropriate (contraindications, precautions, interactions, pregnancy and lactation) -> communicate agreed management plan -> clinical review, with side columns 'Refer when' (11 criteria, p.3) and 'Treat and concurrently refer' (1 criterion, p.3). Table 1 on page 4 lists conditions to exclude (gallstones; peptic ulcer disease/gastritis/Helicobacter pylori infection; myocardial infarction). Definition used (p.3): GORD symptoms frequent (2 or more episodes per week) or severe enough to significantly impair quality of life, or complications present. No molecule, strength, dose or frequency is printed: pharmacotherapy is 'as per the Therapeutic Guidelines: Gastrointestinal (Gastro-oesophageal reflux in adults)', with the printed anchors being '8 weeks of PPI therapy at the standard dose' (referral criterion, p.3) and follow-up 4 to 8 weeks after initiating new therapy (p.7). Total quantity prescribed (including repeats) must not exceed 12 months' supply (p.7).

inclusion.text: Service restricted to patients aged 18 to 55 years.
Initial patient eligibility and suitability for management within the scope of the service (first step of the guideline overview flow).
Patient informed consent (including consent for communication with other health practitioners if relevant).
Patient history and assessment completed: 'Obtain sufficient information from the patient to assess the safety and appropriateness of any recommendations and medicines.'
Examination completed: 'Where appropriate, conduct assessment of vital signs.'

Presentation is not better explained by a condition listed in Table 1: Some conditions with symptoms similar to gastro-oesophageal reflux (gallstones; peptic ulcer disease/gastritis/Helicobacter pylori infection; myocardial infarction) - i.e. those conditions have been excluded ('Conditions to exclude').
The patient does not meet any of the 11 'Refer when' criteria listed on page 3 (confirm before managing within the service).

Symptoms meet the Therapeutic Guidelines definition of GORD used by this document: 'gastro-oesophageal reflux symptoms that are frequent (2 or more episodes per week) or severe enough to significantly impair quality of life, or if complications of gastro-oesophageal reflux are present'. Diagnosis is presumptive and clinical, based on patient reported symptoms; response to a trial of PPIs can help confirm the diagnosis.

exclusion.text: the patient is aged below 18 or above 55 years (does not preclude a patient from accessing usual pharmacy care)
chest pain as the primary symptom
symptoms of anaemia, including fatigue, shortness of breath, weakness, dizziness, or an irregular heartbeat
prolonged or recurrent vomiting (longer than 24 to 48 hours)
inadequate response to optimal treatment (8 weeks of PPI therapy at the standard dose).

exclusion_exceptions.text: Ineligibility for treatment as part of a prescribing service does not preclude a patient from accessing services provided as part of usual pharmacy care.
(does not preclude a patient from accessing usual pharmacy care) [printed against EXC-1, 'the patient is aged below 18 or above 55 years']

steps.description: Meet service and professional obligations - 'Initial patient eligibility and suitability for management within the scope of the service'. Scope: 'Service restricted to patients aged 18 to 55 years.' Screen against the 'Refer when' list (11 criteria, page 3): 'Refer the patient to an appropriate healthcare provider (including emergency services, if required) in the following situations...'. 'Ineligibility for treatment as part of a prescribing service does not preclude a patient from accessing services provided as part of usual pharmacy care.'

gates.criterion: Patient aged 18 to 55 years inclusive
Patient is suitable for management within the scope of the service and meets none of the 11 'Refer when' criteria (page 3)

steps.description: Obtain 'Patient informed consent (including consent for communication with other health practitioners if relevant)'.

gates.criterion: Informed consent obtained, including consent for communication with other health practitioners if relevant

steps.description: Patient history and assessment. 'Obtain sufficient information from the patient to assess the safety and appropriateness of any recommendations and medicines.' Presenting signs and symptoms (p.4): 'The clinical symptoms of GORD are common to multiple other conditions but can often be differentiated using the patient's history.' In addition to the cardinal signs of heartburn and regurgitation other atypical symptoms attributed to reflux include: belching; epigastric pain; dyspepsia; acid brash (saliva mixing with stomach acid in the mouth); early post-prandial satiety. Extra-oesophageal symptoms that are associated with, but not specific to, gastro-oesophageal reflux may include: tooth sensitivity, enamel erosion (particularly on palatal surface of upper incisors), and halitosis; pharyngeal and laryngeal signs and symptoms such as hoarseness and throat clearing, persistent cough, sore throat, pharyngitis, and sinusitis; chest pain; sleep disturbance; nausea; asthma-like symptoms (cough, wheeze, shortness of breath). The patient history (p.5) should consider: age; weight; pregnancy and lactation status (if applicable); nature, severity, and frequency of symptoms (typical, atypical, and extra-oesophageal), including signs and symptoms that may indicate the need for referral; onset and duration of symptoms; precipitating and relieving factors; underlying medical conditions and conditions that may complicate diagnosis e.g. coronary heart disease and asthma; dietary patterns or changes; current and recently ceased treatments (including prescribed medicines, vitamins, herbs, other supplements, and over-the-counter medicines); allergies/adverse drug reactions; pharmacological and non-pharmacological (dietary and lifestyle) strategies tried to treat current symptoms; alcohol and drug history; smoking status. 'Pharmacists can access a range of clinical information in a patient's My Health Record, including details about current and past medication history, allergies, and current medical conditions.'

gates.criterion: History identifies no signs and symptoms that may indicate the need for referral (the 11 'Refer when' criteria on page 3)
Sufficient information obtained to assess the safety and appropriateness of any recommendations and medicines

steps.description: Examination - 'Where appropriate, conduct assessment of vital signs.'

gates.criterion: Vital signs assessed where appropriate (no values, thresholds or 'appropriate' definition printed)

steps.description: Conditions to exclude - 'Table 1: Some conditions with symptoms similar to gastro-oesophageal reflux' with differentiating features: Gallstones (nausea and vomiting; intense epigastric or right upper quadrant pain, which may radiate to the back, shoulder, or arm); Peptic ulcer disease/gastritis/Helicobacter pylori infection (abdominal pain; nausea; unintentional weight loss; melena); Myocardial infarction (nausea; pressure, tightness, pain, or aching sensation in chest or arms that may spread to neck, jaw, or back; shortness of breath; cold sweats; fatigue). '*This table does not list all possible conditions or features. Consult specialised references for further information.' Diagnosis: 'The presumptive clinical diagnosis of gastro-oesophageal reflux and GORD are primarily based on patient reported symptoms. However, response to a trial of proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) can help to confirm a diagnosis of GORD. A trial of high dose PPIs has a sensitivity of 80 per cent as a diagnostic test for GORD.' 'The fundamental signs of gastro-oesophageal reflux are heartburn and regurgitation.'

gates.criterion: Presentation is not better explained by a condition in Table 1 (gallstones; peptic ulcer disease/gastritis/Helicobacter pylori infection; myocardial infarction)

Diagnosis supported by patient reported symptoms (heartburn and regurgitation; frequent 2 or more episodes per week, or impairing quality of life, or complications present) and/or response to a trial of PPIs

steps.description: Develop management plan. 'Pharmacists must ensure that they are prescribing medicines according to the specified sections of the current online version of the Therapeutic Guidelines.' 'The initial management of gastro-oesophageal reflux and GORD is based on the severity of symptoms; symptom control is the aim for most patients.' Pharmacist management involves: non-pharmacological measures - advice regarding dietary and lifestyle modification as per the Therapeutic Guidelines: Diet and lifestyle modification for the management of gastro-oesophageal reflux in adults; pharmacotherapy - as per the Therapeutic Guidelines: Gastrointestinal (Gastro-oesophageal reflux in adults). 'Mild intermittent symptoms may be managed with diet and lifestyle modification only. However, on-demand (when required) drug therapy may also be used if symptoms are significantly troublesome.' NB1: 'The efficacy and availability of PPIs has led to overuse. Long-term regular PPI therapy is only recommended for a limited number of indications and should be reviewed regularly.' NB2: 'Where regular drug therapy is required, consider referral to an appropriate healthcare provider.'

gates.criterion: Treatment matched to symptom severity (mild intermittent: diet and lifestyle modification only, with on-demand drug therapy permitted if symptoms are significantly troublesome)
Long-term regular PPI therapy is limited to one of the 'limited number of indications' and will be reviewed regularly (NB1)
Where regular drug therapy is required, referral to an appropriate healthcare provider has been considered (NB2)

steps.description: Confirm management is appropriate - 'Consult the Therapeutic Guidelines, Australian Medicines Handbook and other resources to confirm that management is appropriate, including for: contraindications and precautions; drug interactions; pregnancy and lactation.'

gates.criterion: No contraindications or precautions identified for the proposed treatment
No drug interactions identified for the proposed treatment
Pregnancy and lactation status considered and management confirmed appropriate

steps.description: Communicate agreed management plan. 'Comprehensive advice and counselling (including supporting written information when required) should be provided to the patient regarding: individual medicine use e.g. initial dosing, maintenance, and step-down therapy; non-pharmacological measures; how to manage adverse effects; when to seek further care and/or treatment; when to return for follow-up.' 'It is the pharmacist's responsibility to ensure the suitability and accuracy of any resources and information provided to patients (and/or parents/caregivers), and to ensure compliance with all copyright conditions.' 'The agreed management plan should be shared with members of the patient's multidisciplinary healthcare team, with the patient's consent.' General advice: 'At the time of initial consultation, patients (and/or parents/caregivers) should be advised to see an appropriate healthcare provider if: the condition does not improve with recommended treatment (e.g. within 8 weeks of starting treatment with a PPI); ongoing maintenance treatment with a PPI is required; the patient's condition worsens, including developing systemic signs and symptoms; the patient develops new or changed signs or symptoms; adverse effects of treatment cannot be managed in the pharmacy setting.'

gates.criterion: Agreed management plan communicated (medicine use, non-pharmacological measures, adverse effects, when to seek further care, when to return for follow-up) and shared with the multidisciplinary healthcare team with consent; all five general advice triggers advised at the initial consultation

steps.description: Clinical review. 'Clinical review with the pharmacist (or the patient's chosen healthcare provider) should occur in line with recommendations in the Therapeutic Guidelines.' 'Patients should return for a follow up consultation 4 to 8 weeks after initiation of a new therapy to assess: adherence to pharmacotherapy and non-pharmacological management strategies; response to treatment and if changes to the treatment plan are required (continue, modify, stop, and/or refer).' 'For patients continuing therapy, the frequency of further follow up appointments for maintenance and step-down therapy should be individualised to the patient's clinical presentation, response to treatment, and therapeutic goals, and based on recommendations in the Therapeutic Guidelines.' 'Pharmacists should prescribe a quantity of medicine (including repeats), that aligns with the expected duration of therapy, ensuring sufficient supply until the patient's next review. The total quantity prescribed should not exceed 12 months' supply (including repeats).'

gates.criterion: Follow up consultation held 4 to 8 weeks after initiation of a new therapy (adherence and response assessed)

diagnosis_pathways.name: Refer when / treat and concurrently refer triage (page 3), with general advice on when to seek further care (page 6)

steps.description: Screen against the 'Refer when' criteria: 'Refer the patient to an appropriate healthcare provider (including emergency services, if required) in the following situations: the patient is aged below 18 or above 55 years (does not preclude a patient from accessing usual pharmacy care); unclear diagnosis; chest pain as the primary symptom; symptoms of anaemia, including fatigue, shortness of breath, weakness, dizziness, or an irregular heartbeat; difficulty or painful swallowing; prolonged or recurrent vomiting (longer than 24 to 48 hours); jaundice; haematemesis or melaena; unexplained weight loss; severe, frequent, or changing symptoms; inadequate response to optimal treatment (8 weeks of PPI therapy at the standard dose).'

gates.criterion: None of the 11 'Refer when' criteria is present

steps.description: Refer the patient to an appropriate healthcare provider (including emergency services, if required). No urgency tier or destination is printed for any individual criterion; the document states only the generic '(including emergency services, if required)'.

gates.criterion: Referral destination and urgency arranged (not specified in the document)

steps.description: 'Treat (if clinically appropriate) and concurrently refer - Patient is on a medication that can precipitate reflux.'

gates.criterion: Where the patient is on a medication that can precipitate reflux: initial treatment provided (if clinically appropriate) AND concurrent referral to an appropriate healthcare provider made

provenance.section_heading: Treat (if clinically appropriate) and concurrently refer

steps.description: General advice - 'At the time of initial consultation, patients (and/or parents/caregivers) should be advised to see an appropriate healthcare provider if: the condition does not improve with recommended treatment (e.g. within 8 weeks of starting treatment with a PPI); ongoing maintenance treatment with a PPI is required; the patient's condition worsens, including developing systemic signs and symptoms; the patient develops new or changed signs or symptoms; adverse effects of treatment cannot be managed in the pharmacy setting.'

gates.criterion: All five 'see an appropriate healthcare provider if' triggers have been advised at the initial consultation

treatments.strength: 'standard dose' and 'high dose' are referred to but not defined; no molecule, product or strength printed
treatments.frequency: on-demand (when required) drug therapy is permitted if symptoms are significantly troublesome; otherwise 'as per the Therapeutic Guidelines: Gastrointestinal (Gastro-oesophageal reflux in adults)' - no frequency printed
treatments.duration: 8 weeks of PPI therapy at the standard dose (printed as the definition of 'optimal treatment' for the refer-when criterion 'inadequate response to optimal treatment'); long-term regular PPI therapy 'should be reviewed regularly'
treatments.max_quantity: The total quantity prescribed should not exceed 12 months' supply (including repeats) (p.7).
treatments.quantity_to_supply: quantity aligned with the expected duration of therapy, ensuring sufficient supply until the patient's next review; total quantity prescribed (including repeats) must not exceed 12 months' supply
treatments.notes: 'Pharmacotherapy: as per the Therapeutic Guidelines: Gastrointestinal (Gastro-oesophageal reflux in adults)' (p.6) - no molecule, dose, frequency, route, device or quantity is printed in this protocol, so TX-1 dose/frequency/max_dose are blank. Printed PPI statements transcribed verbatim: 'response to a trial of proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) can help to confirm a diagnosis of GORD'; 'A trial of high dose PPIs has a sensitivity of 80 per cent as a diagnostic test for GORD' (p.3); 'The efficacy and availability of PPIs has led to overuse. Long-term regular PPI therapy is only recommended for a limited number of indications and should be reviewed regularly' (NB1, p.6); 'Where regular drug therapy is required, consider referral to an appropriate healthcare provider' (NB2, p.6); refer-when trigger 'inadequate response to optimal treatment (8 weeks of PPI therapy at the standard dose)' (p.3); general advice trigger 'the condition does not improve with recommended treatment (e.g. within 8 weeks of starting treatment with a PPI)' and 'ongoing maintenance treatment with a PPI is required' (p.6). Severity-based use: 'Mild intermittent symptoms may be managed with diet and lifestyle modification only. However, on-demand (when required) drug therapy may also be used if symptoms are significantly troublesome' (p.3). Pregnancy/lactation: confirm management is appropriate including for pregnancy and lactation (p.6); no pregnancy-specific prescribing restriction or referral rule is printed for this condition. Supply: quantity (including repeats) aligns with expected duration, sufficient until next review, total not exceeding 12 months' supply (p.7).

'non-pharmacological measures: advice regarding dietary and lifestyle modification as per the Therapeutic Guidelines: Diet and lifestyle modification for the management of gastro-oesophageal reflux in adults' (p.6). 'Mild intermittent symptoms may be managed with diet and lifestyle modification only' (p.3); 'The initial management of gastro-oesophageal reflux and GORD is based on the severity of symptoms; symptom control is the aim for most patients.' Assessment includes 'pharmacological and non-pharmacological (dietary and lifestyle) strategies tried to treat current symptoms' and 'dietary patterns or changes' (p.5). No specific dietary instruction, frequency or duration is printed in this document; the content is external (Therapeutic Guidelines).

open_questions.topic: Ambiguous vomiting threshold: 'longer than 24 to 48 hours'
open_questions.observed: 'prolonged or recurrent vomiting (longer than 24 to 48 hours)' is printed as a refer-when criterion (p.3, repeated in the p.2 flow column).
open_questions.why_unclear: 'Longer than 24 to 48 hours' does not identify a single cut-off (24 hours or 48 hours, or a range between them). EXC-6 and RF-6 are transcribed verbatim with confidence 'unclear' and structured null; hugh_to_confirm asks which threshold to encode.

open_questions.topic: Combinatorics of the eligibility decision list are not printed
open_questions.observed: The guideline prints an eligibility flow (p.2) with sequential boxes and the referral list as 'in the following situations:' (p.3); no explicit AND/OR statement appears anywhere.
open_questions.why_unclear: Inclusion criteria were given all_of (each flow box plus the age, differential-diagnosis and definition requirements must hold); exclusion criteria were given any_of because 'in the following situations' reads as any one triggering referral. Confidence on the inclusion members is therefore 'medium' rather than 'high'.

open_questions.topic: Two-column layout on page 2 - ordering reconstructed
open_questions.observed: Page 2 prints the flow ('Meet service and professional obligations' ... 'Clinical review') in the left column and 'Refer when' / 'Treat and concurrently refer' in the right column; the flat text extraction interleaves the two columns line by line.
open_questions.why_unclear: Content was reassembled by column and cross-checked against the full lists printed on page 3 (the right column of page 2 repeats page 3 verbatim). No criterion text is affected; only the reading order of the p.2 flow could differ if printed row-wise.

open_questions.topic: No molecule, strength, dose, frequency or quantity printed for pharmacotherapy
open_questions.observed: 'pharmacotherapy: as per the Therapeutic Guidelines: Gastrointestinal (Gastro-oesophageal reflux in adults)'; 'Pharmacists must ensure that they are prescribing medicines according to the specified sections of the current online version of the Therapeutic Guidelines.' The only printed medicine anchors are PPI class references, 'standard dose', 'high dose' and '8 weeks of PPI therapy at the standard dose'.
open_questions.why_unclear: TX-1 has blank dose/route/max_dose fields; 'standard dose' and 'high dose' are undefined in this document, so neither the treatment regimen nor the EXC-11/RF-11 8-week rule can be evaluated numerically without the external guideline.

open_questions.topic: Table 1 conditions to exclude carry no printed action or urgency
open_questions.observed: 'Conditions to exclude - Table 1: Some conditions with symptoms similar to gastro-oesophageal reflux' lists gallstones, peptic ulcer disease/gastritis/Helicobacter pylori infection and myocardial infarction with differentiating features, and footnotes '*This table does not list all possible conditions or features. Consult specialised references for further information.' No referral instruction or urgency is attached to the table.
open_questions.why_unclear: RF-19 to RF-21 record the three rows as referral triggers with action REFER (via the printed refer-when criterion 'unclear diagnosis') and severity 'medium' (the document's plain referral level); severity was deliberately NOT upgraded for the myocardial infarction row because no urgency language is printed. The gate on PW-1-S5 is recorded with the same medium confidence.

open_questions.topic: No urgency tiers are printed for any referral criterion
open_questions.observed: The 'Refer when' preamble reads 'Refer the patient to an appropriate healthcare provider (including emergency services, if required)' but no individual criterion is tagged urgent or emergency, and the document contains no ambulance/000 instruction.
open_questions.why_unclear: referral.urgent is left empty because the document genuinely prints no urgent-tier item; all refer-when red flags were given severity 'medium' and severity was not upgraded beyond the document's own language. The generic emergency-services wording is recorded once in referral.emergency.

open_questions.observed: Inclusion side states 'Service restricted to patients aged 18 to 55 years' (p.1); exclusion side states 'the patient is aged below 18 or above 55 years' (p.3). Both readings agree that 18 and 55 are inclusive.
open_questions.why_unclear: No ambiguity found; recorded to document that age_bounds 18/55 is the printed pair.

open_questions.topic: Gate on_fail not stated for several pathway gates
open_questions.observed: The document does not state what happens when consent cannot be obtained (PW-1-S2), when history is insufficient (PW-1-S3), when vital signs are not assessed (PW-1-S4), when the diagnosis is not confirmed by symptoms/PPI trial (PW-1-S5), when severity-matching, NB1 or NB2 fail (PW-1-S6), when any confirm-management check fails (PW-1-S7), when the plan cannot be communicated (PW-1-S8), when the 4-8 week follow-up is missed (PW-1-S9), or when referral destination/urgency cannot be arranged (PW-2-S2).
open_questions.why_unclear: Spec requires on_fail 'unclear' plus an open question where the document is silent; these are recorded as 'unclear' rather than inferred. Age, refer-when screening, differential-diagnosis exclusion and treat-and-concurrent-referral do have printed consequences and are encoded as REFER.

open_questions.topic: Pregnancy and lactation: confirmation required but no action printed
open_questions.observed: 'Confirm management is appropriate - ... including for: contraindications and precautions; drug interactions; pregnancy and lactation' (p.6). Unlike some EACPP guidelines, this document's 'Refer when' and 'Treat and concurrently refer' lists contain no pregnancy item.
open_questions.why_unclear: PW-1-S7 therefore records pregnancy/lactation as a confirmation gate with on_fail 'unclear'; no referral or dose change for pregnancy can be transcribed without inventing it.

open_questions.topic: Definition of the GORD threshold used as inclusion INC-8
open_questions.observed: 'The Therapeutic Guidelines defines gastro-oesophageal reflux disease (GORD) as gastro-oesophageal reflux symptoms that are frequent (2 or more episodes per week) or severe enough to significantly impair quality of life, or if complications of gastro-oesophageal reflux are present' (p.3).
open_questions.why_unclear: The document does not state that patients below this frequency are ineligible for the service, so INC-8 is recorded with confidence 'medium' as a diagnostic-definition requirement rather than a hard eligibility cut-off.

open_questions.topic: Referral block provenance spans pages 2, 3 and 6
open_questions.observed: Referral destinations and criteria appear on page 2 (flow columns), page 3 (the full lists), page 4 (conditions to exclude) and page 6 (NB2 and general advice).
open_questions.why_unclear: Spec allows one shared provenance for the referral block using the first page of the full list; page 3 recorded, with the range noted here.

open_questions.topic: No version number or effective date printed
open_questions.observed: Page 9 footer codes read "62'GUA" and "180510-DEC"; the document shows © Department of Health 2026, 'Produced by Clinical Excellence Division', and references up to 2025/2026 sources, but no protocol version/date.
open_questions.why_unclear: instrument_version and effective_date could not be filled from a printed identifier.

open_questions.topic: Consent documentation content is not specified
open_questions.observed: 'Patient informed consent (including consent for communication with other health practitioners if relevant)' (p.2) is required, but no consent form, wording or record location is printed in this document.
open_questions.why_unclear: PW-1-S2 gate on_fail is recorded as 'unclear' and the consent content must come from Pilot materials outside this protocol.

open_questions.topic: No notifiable-condition, AIR or GP-notification requirement printed
open_questions.observed: The only communication obligations are consent-gated plan sharing with the multidisciplinary healthcare team (p.6) and 'Communication with other health practitioners' as a flow step (p.2).
open_questions.why_unclear: notifiable.required is set true for those consent-gated communication duties only; no notifiable condition, AIR upload or mandatory GP notification appears anywhere in the document.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Encode PPI molecule(s), standard dose, high dose, route, frequency and duration from the current online Therapeutic Guidelines: Gastrointestinal (Gastro-oesophageal reflux in adults) - none are printed in this protocol.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: TX-1 is the only pharmacotherapy row and has blank dose/route/max_dose fields; a prescribing support module cannot issue supply instructions from this instrument alone.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm how the refer-when rule 'inadequate response to optimal treatment (8 weeks of PPI therapy at the standard dose)' is evaluated: which molecule/dose counts as 'the standard dose', what counts as adequate response, and whether the clock starts at initiation or at last dose change.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: This is the document's only time-based automatic referral trigger (RF-11, structured >= 8 weeks) and it cannot fire without a defined standard dose and response measure.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Resolve the ambiguous vomiting threshold 'longer than 24 to 48 hours' - choose 24 hours, 48 hours, or a documented range before go-live (recorded as EXC-6/RF-6 with confidence 'unclear' and structured null).
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Two readings are possible and they produce different referral behaviour for a patient vomiting 30 hours.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Define which medicines count as 'a medication that can precipitate reflux' for the treat-and-concurrently-refer criterion (no list is printed).
hugh_to_confirm.reason: RF-12 can only fire if the offending-medicine class is enumerated locally; the document gives no drugs, no de-prescribing instruction and no alternative-treatment advice.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Encode NB1 as a prescribing constraint: 'Long-term regular PPI therapy is only recommended for a limited number of indications and should be reviewed regularly' - obtain the list of indications and review interval from Therapeutic Guidelines: Gastrointestinal.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Without the indication list the engine cannot distinguish supported long-term PPI therapy from the overuse the guideline warns against.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Decide whether NB2 ('Where regular drug therapy is required, consider referral to an appropriate healthcare provider') is advisory or a hard gate in the module.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: The document says 'consider', so RF-18 was recorded at severity low; if the business rule is mandatory referral, the encoding must change.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm local process for the four-or-eight-week review cadence and how it interacts with the 8-week no-improvement referral trigger: follow-up is '4 to 8 weeks after initiation of a new therapy' while non-improvement 'within 8 weeks' triggers referral.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: The same 8-week window is both a review point and a referral threshold; precedence must be decided locally so patients are not referred before the scheduled review or reviewed after the referral point.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm the local supply policy for the printed cap: 'The total quantity prescribed should not exceed 12 months' supply (including repeats)' and quantity aligned with expected duration until next review.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Quantity-to-supply depends on the local review schedule; the 12-month ceiling is the only printed cap and must be enforced at dispensing.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm what 'Where appropriate, conduct assessment of vital signs' requires in practice (which vital signs, any thresholds, and what makes it 'appropriate') - no values or thresholds are printed.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: PW-1-S4 is a required examination step but is unenforceable as written; local policy must supply the parameters.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm how findings from 'Conditions to exclude' (Table 1: gallstones; peptic ulcer disease/gastritis/Helicobacter pylori infection; myocardial infarction) are handled - the table prints no action or urgency and states it 'does not list all possible conditions or features'.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: RF-19 to RF-21 were assigned action REFER with severity medium via 'unclear diagnosis'; escalation (especially for possible myocardial infarction) must be confirmed because the document does not grade urgency.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm pharmacist EACPP approval and authorisation status per the Medicines and Poisons Regulations 2016 (WA): 'This document alone does not provide an authorisation for a pharmacist to prescribe.'
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Prescribing under the protocol is conditional on individual Department of Health approval, which is not verifiable from the document.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Obtain the consent documentation requirements for participation, including consent for communication with other health practitioners (no consent wording or form is printed in this document).
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Consent is a gating step (PW-1-S2) and also the condition attached to sharing the management plan (notifiable.conditions), but its required content and record format are external.
